references.text: The Passover lamb was to be slaughtered on the fourteenth day of the first month, which is the same date mentioned in Numbers 28:16.
Confirms that the Passover celebration begins on the fourteenth day of the first month.
Parallel law text establishing Passover for the fourteenth day of the first month.
Moses repeats the command to keep Passover in the month of Aviv (the first month).
The Israelites celebrated Passover on the fourteenth day of the first month after entering Canaan.
King Josiah kept Passover for the Lord, and the Passover lamb was slaughtered on the fourteenth day of the first month.
The returned exiles celebrated Passover on the fourteenth day of the first month.
Ezekiel's vision confirms the celebration of Passover on the fourteenth day of the first month.
Jesus and his disciples prepared the Passover meal on the first day of the Feast of Unleavened Bread, which is linked to the fourteenth of Nisan.
Jesus was crucified on the day of preparation for Passover, linking his death to the Passover lamb.
Paul calls Christ our Passover lamb who has been sacrificed, linking Passover to Christ's sacrifice.
